title: Durga
shortLine: A woman survives the night, then must live through its morning.
synopsis: Durga has learned to disguise suffering as tiredness inside a home ruled by Inspector Nitin Sobhraj, a man whose public respectability protects his private cruelty. Haunted by Raj’s death and by visions that offer both comfort and accusation, she is forced to face the terrible distance between the man the city admires and the monster who owns her life.
imageAlt: A dim bedroom with a ceiling fan and bed, an ordinary domestic space.
imageCredit: Unsplash — Rupam Dhar; photo page linked in UNSPLASH-SOURCES.txt.
detailLine: The city trusts the man who breaks her. The morning asks her to make his tea.
underneath: The horror is not hidden in a distant supernatural place; it lives inside an ordinary home and is sustained by silence. The visions of Raj blur comfort with guilt, while the city’s routine reveals how violence can coexist with public respectability.
visualMotifs: A red dress torn against a grey room
An olive shirt carrying the memory of love
A ceiling fan turning without pause
A newspaper in the morning sun
A dead bat on the floor
coreQuestion: When everyone around a victim keeps ordinary life moving, does their silence remain neutrality—or become part of the violence?

detailImage.alt: A dark, spare room receives a hard shaft of daylight through its window.
detailImage.caption: Morning returns to a house that has not become safe.
